newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Top developments on Thursday in Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: Top developments on Thursday in Zaire crisis.

text.p: Following are top developments on Thursday in the crisis in eastern Zaire:
--Rwandan refugees are dying of thirst in the harsh mountains of east Zaire, U.N. officials said quoting some of the first eyewitness accounts from the war-ravaged region.

--In Kinshasa, thousands of students calling for the resignation of part-Tutsi Prime Minister Kenga wa Dongo took over Zaire's parliament building, bringing with them the coffins of two students killed in earlier protests.
--Zaire war refugees began arriving in Kisangani, Zaire on swollen feet after fleeing the fighting far to the east, aid officials said.
--In Madrid, Spain condemned the international community for neglecting dire problems in central Africa for years and also criticised regional leaders such as South African President Nelson Mandela.
--In Rome, the head of the Organisation of African Unity urged the United Nations to back international intervention to save war refugees in Zaire and said Washington had an important role to play.

--In Brussels, European Union aid ministers, stung by French criticism of "spineless inaction" in the plight of 1.2 million refugees stranded in eastern Zaire, struggled to find a joint response to the deepening human crisis.
